chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from one of our companions, from Salih ibn Hamza, from one of our companions who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is upon you to correct/manage the wealth, for therein is a stimulant for the benevolent and a self-sufficiency from the wicked ones'.

key_terms.اللَّئِيمِ: The mean/wicked/poor person (contextually: those from whom one seeks or is dependent)
key_terms.مَنْبَهَةٌ: Stimulant, incentive, or means of encouragement

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and social benefit of managing one's wealth correctly according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes that the rectification of wealth (*islah al-mal*) is not merely financial but spiritual, serving as a catalyst for noble character. By ensuring one's resources are properly managed and purified, an individual achieves *istighna* (self-sufficiency), which preserves dignity and reduces dependence on others, thereby fostering generosity and reducing the need to seek favor from the less virtuous.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad, from one of our companions, from Salih Bin Hamza, from one of our companions who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is upon you with the correction of the wealth, for therein is a stimulant for the benevolent and a self-sufficiency from the wicked ones’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from him (narrator of previous Fladith) from certain persons of our people from Salih ibn Hamzah from certain persons of our people Hamzah who have said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘You must manage your wealth properly; it increases respect for you and freedom of want from envious ones.’”
